Summarize a heterogeneous transition network

Source: R/summary_htna.R
summary.htna.Rd

summary() summarizes a heterogeneous transition network by its actor partition; print() shows the summary and as.data.frame() returns its tables. A heterogeneous transition network is described first by which codes belong to which actor type, and how the transitions between codes fall within and between the actors. The summary reports the network's size (sessions, nodes and non-zero edges), the nodes of each actor, the number of non-zero edges in every directed actor-pair block (for example Human to AI), and the standard network-level descriptive metrics (density, mean distance, strength, degree centralization and reciprocity). In an undirected network (method = "co_occurrence") every edge is counted once, so the blocks are the unordered actor pairs.

summary() returns the summary as a summary.htna object; printing it shows the report. For a grouped network, the summary of every cohort is returned and printed in turn. The tables of the summary are returned as data frames by as.data.frame().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'htna'
summary(object, max_nodes = 12L, ...)

# S3 method for class 'htna_group'
summary(object, max_nodes = 12L, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.htna'
print(x, max_nodes = attr(x, "max_nodes") %||% 12L, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.htna_group'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.htna'
as.data.frame(
  x,
  row.names = NULL,
  optional = FALSE,
  ...,
  what = c("actors", "actor_pairs", "metrics")
)

# S3 method for class 'summary.htna_group'
as.data.frame(
  x,
  row.names = NULL,
  optional = FALSE,
  ...,
  what = c("actors", "actor_pairs", "metrics")
)

Arguments

object

An htna network from build_htna() or an htna_group.

max_nodes

Maximum number of nodes listed per actor type when the summary is printed (default 12).

...

Unused.

x

A summary.htna or summary.htna_group object.

row.names, optional

Ignored; present for the generic.

what

Table to return: "actors" (default; one row per actor type with its number of nodes and their names), "actor_pairs" (one row per directed actor pair with the number of non-zero edges; one row per unordered pair for an undirected network) or "metrics" (one row per network metric).

Value

summary() returns an object of class summary.htna: a list with actors (data frame: actor, n_nodes, nodes), edges_by_actor (integer matrix of non-zero edge counts, source actors in rows; symmetric for an undirected network), network_metrics (data frame: metric, value), and the scalars n_nodes, n_edges, directed, n_sessions, n_timesteps and method. For an htna_group it returns a summary.htna_group, a named list of summary.htna objects. print() returns its input invisibly. as.data.frame() returns the table chosen by what; for a grouped summary the cohorts are stacked with a leading group column.

See also

build_htna(), as.data.frame.htna() for the edge and node tables of the network itself.

Examples

data(human_ai)
net <- build_htna(human_ai, actor_type = "actor_type")
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'session_date' (1 sessions), 'cluster' (42 sessions), 'actor_type' (24 sessions)
summary(net)
#> <htna network>
#>   Method:    relative
#>   Sessions:  429   (max 287 timesteps)
#>   Nodes:     12
#>   Edges:     135 / 144 (non-zero)
#> 
#> Actor types (2):
#>   Human (6 nodes):  Check, Frustrate, Inquire, Refine, Request, Specify
#>   AI    (6 nodes):  Ask, Delegate, Execute, Plan, Repair, Report
#> 
#> Edge counts by actor (rows = source, cols = target):
#>           Human    AI
#>   Human      35    36
#>   AI         36    28
#> 
#> Network metrics:
#>                       metric        value
#>                   Node Count  12.00000000
#>                   Edge Count 135.00000000
#>              Network Density   1.00000000
#>                Mean Distance   0.02743124
#>            Mean Out-Strength   1.00000000
#>              SD Out-Strength   0.00000000
#>             Mean In-Strength   1.00000000
#>               SD In-Strength   0.63085045
#>              Mean Out-Degree  11.25000000
#>                SD Out-Degree   0.96530730
#>  Centralization (Out-Degree)   0.05785124
#>   Centralization (In-Degree)   0.05785124
#>                  Reciprocity   0.96000000
as.data.frame(summary(net), what = "actor_pairs")
#>   source_actor target_actor n_edges
#> 1        Human        Human      35
#> 2        Human           AI      36
#> 3           AI        Human      36
#> 4           AI           AI      28

grp <- build_htna(human_ai, actor_type = "actor_type", group = "phase")
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'cluster' (24 sessions), 'actor_type' (9 sessions)
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'session_date' (1 sessions), 'cluster' (18 sessions), 'actor_type' (15 sessions)
as.data.frame(summary(grp), what = "metrics")
#>    group                      metric        value
#> 1  Early                  Node Count 1.200000e+01
#> 2  Early                  Edge Count 1.350000e+02
#> 3  Early             Network Density 1.000000e+00
#> 4  Early               Mean Distance 2.704448e-02

#> 10 Early               SD Out-Degree 9.653073e-01
#> 11 Early Centralization (Out-Degree) 5.785124e-02
#> 12 Early  Centralization (In-Degree) 5.785124e-02
#> 13 Early                 Reciprocity 9.600000e-01
